title: Inspect and extend: Content rules and private-mode clearing
objective: Use the real implementation in `Sources/Core.swift` to demonstrate and safely improve rule-list json, rule compilation, blocked-count reporting, and private data behavior.
problem: A rule list is a set of instructions sent to WebKit’s content blocker. Follow its JSON shape and how settings select it, then examine tests for private-mode cleanup and tracker counts. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `Sources/Core.swift` and the related project files: Sources/Core.swift; Sources/Models.swift; Sources/Screens/SettingsView.swift; Tests/BrowserCoreTests.swift.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to rule-list json, rule compilation, blocked-count reporting, and private data behavior.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: The sample rules are limited; a counter is not proof that every tracker was blocked.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A rule list is a set of instructions sent to WebKit’s content blocker. Follow its JSON shape and how settings select it, then examine tests for private-mode cleanup and tracker counts.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `Sources/Core.swift`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
